findings.claim: `failureCode` is validated only as a closed enum and is never constrained by `outcome`/`dispatchedAt`, so a `refused_before_dispatch` receipt that by contract never reached the provider may still be classified `provider_error`, `timeout` or `unknown_after_dispatch`, and the report then prints those codes next to `dispatched: 0` — the same writer's-free-choice ambiguity between pre- and post-dispatch facts that the two round-0 lifecycle findings closed for `failureLayer`.
findings.reproduction: Take the `refused_before_dispatch` receipt already asserted valid at tests/promptRefinerReceiptCore.test.mjs:63-86 and change only `failureCode` to `"unknown_after_dispatch"` (or `"provider_error"`, or `"timeout"`): `promptRefinerExecutionReceiptSchema.safeParse(...).success` is `true`, and `summarizePromptRefinerReceipts(bundle([thatReceipt], []))` returns `{ dispatched: 0, dispatchedFailures: 0, failureCodes: { unknown_after_dispatch: 1 } }`. Expected, matching the failureLayer rules at :188-196 and :204-208: codes that assert provider contact (`provider_error`, `timeout`, `invalid_response`, `empty_response`, `no_change`, `unknown_after_dispatch`) fail closed when `dispatchedAt === null`, and pre-dispatch codes (`adapter_unavailable`, `cost_guardrail`) fail closed on a dispatched `failed` receipt.

verdict.nextAction: Merge as is; optionally add one predicate partitioning `PROMPT_REFINER_FAILURE_CODES` into pre- and post-dispatch codes keyed on `dispatchedAt`, with a regression case in the existing `invalid` array.
